docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Every skill contribution follows a controlled 9-stage lifecycle. This ensures that skills are developed, reviewed and released consistently without damaging the rest of the system.

docs.title: 1. Intake
docs.text: Contributor selects one change type: - NEW - Create a new skill - UPDATE - Update an existing skill - SUBSKILL - Create a sub-skill under an existing parent - SPLIT - Split mixed content into domain-specific skills - DEPRECATE - Deprecate an obsolete skill with migration plan - STANDARD-UPDATE - Update standard metadata and assess affected skills

docs.title: 2. Repository discovery
docs.text: Search the catalogue, related skills, parent/child relationships, domain maps, standards, rules, agents, workflows and evaluation cases before making changes.

docs.title: 3. Gap assessment
docs.text: Determine whether to: - Update an existing skill - Create a child skill - Create an independent skill - Split mixed content - Reject a duplicate proposal

docs.title: 4. Skill design review
docs.text: Agree on domain, activity, ID, applicability, standards, inputs, outputs, relationships, maturity and acceptance criteria before implementation.

docs.title: 5. Authoring
docs.text: Create or update the skill, templates, references, checklists, deterministic scripts and test fixtures.

docs.title: 6. Integration
docs.text: Update the canonical catalogue, domain maps, skill groups, agent routing, relevant workflow and standards links.

docs.title: 7. Automated validation
docs.text: Validate metadata, references, schemas, group matching, traceability, duplicate content, output contracts and evaluation cases.

docs.title: 8. Independent review
docs.text: Obtain domain expert review. Require additional qualified independent review for safety-critical and security-sensitive changes.

docs.title: 9. Pull request and release
docs.text: Run all CI checks, document evidence, update changelog and maturity, then merge through the approved repository process.

docs.title: Contribution decision matrix
docs.text: Situation Correct action Existing skill covers same domain/activity but is incomplete Update existing skill Existing parent has a narrower reusable activity Create a subskill New domain has genuinely different process or evidence requirement Create new domain skill One skill mixes automotive and aerospace controls Split into domain-specific skills A standard changes edition or status Update standard metadata and assess affected skills Existing skill is obsolete Deprecate with migration plan, not delete Content is only a small instruction, not independent workflow Add to existing skill or references

docs.title: Skill Authoring Guide
docs.text:
1. Scaffold: python scripts/create_skill.py --id axiom-<domain>-<cap> --title "..." --apply (dry-run without --apply).
  2. Fill SKILL.md from skills/_templates/SKILL.template.md -- every section, real workflow, real decision rules, real failure modes.
  3. Add checklists/review.yaml, at least one template, deterministic scripts/ (stdlib-only preferred), tests/ for scripts.
  4. Mark maturity honestly: experimental until proven.
  5. Validate: python scripts/validate_skills.py --skill <id> then full run.
  6. Register: add to skills/catalog.yaml (or re-run scaffold/extend scripts), then python -m axiom_cli skills apply (regenerates index + mirrors).
  7. Run: python -m axiom_cli skills run <id> --objective "..." (dry-run), --apply to write under .axiom/runs/.
  8. Finish with the pipeline: python -m axiom_cli skills apply (one command: enrich -> index -> clients -> validate). Never hand-edit generated files.
  9. Grouping: new skills join groups automatically via id/subdomain/tags rules (see docs/skills/GROUPS.md). If your skill matches no group, widen a rule or add one -- CI enforces 100% coverage.

docs.title: Linking (no duplicates, future tools/sub-skills/steps)
docs.text:
• New skill specializing an existing one? Edit the graph directly in skills/catalog.yaml -- no second file: axiom skills link --set related_skills <id> <others>... (or extends with one base, sub_skills, domain_overlays, platform_overlays). Related back-links are auto-maintained. Same call over MCP: link_skill. Then axiom skills apply to propagate + validate (existence and related-symmetry are hard errors).
  • Link tools via the axiom: block: required_tools, optional_tools, mcp_tools (checked against the live MCP registry at validation time; unknown names warn with a pointer to docs/mcp-tool-backlog.md).
  • Link domain/platform packages via domain_overlays / platform_overlays in the catalog entry (must match a directory under domains/ / platforms/).
  • Custom steps/requirements: add them to the SKILL.md Workflow/Inputs sections and mirror machine-checkable gates in checklists/ + scripts/.
  • Consumers needing JSON: axiom skills manifest <id> (derived, never stored -- see docs/skill-manifest-decision.md).

docs.title: Skill groups (smart views for 1000+ skills)
docs.text: Groups are named rules evaluated against skills/catalog.yaml, not folders. Nothing moves on disk when the library grows past 1000 skills: a new skill joins its groups automatically when its id, subdomain, domain, tags, or maturity matches a rule.

docs.title: Rules (skills/groups.yaml)
docs.text:
groups:
  diagnostics:
    title: Vehicle diagnostics
    match_any:                       # OR across clauses ...
      - {subdomain: [diagnostics]}   # ... AND across keys, OR within a list
      - {id: [automotive-diagnostics]}

Match keys: id, id_prefix, domain, subdomain, tags, maturity. Unknown keys are a hard error (ValueError), so typos fail fast.

Invariant (CI-enforced): every enabled catalog skill matches >= 1 group. validate_groups() returns violations; sync_skill_index hard-errors on them; .pre-commit + nightly drift keep it green. If you add a skill that matches nothing, either widen a rule or add a group -- never leave it orphaned.

docs.title: Using groups
docs.text:
Surface Usage Engage (scoped discovery) axiom engage --group diagnostics [--domain automotive] [--limit 20] MCP engage tool with group / limit (total, truncated in reply) Install (copy subset) axiom install --client opencode --groups diagnostics,safety-security Index registries/skill-index.json -> by_group (matcher == index, tested)

--groups ANDs with --domains: a skill copies only if it passes both filters (domains=[all] shared skills always pass the domain side). --limit 0 (default) means all; any positive cap sets truncated: true and reports total so agents can page.

docs.title: Adding a group (no code change)
docs.text:
1. Append to skills/groups.yaml under groups:.
  2. Run axiom skills apply -- index, by_group, and mirrors regenerate.
  3. CI (pipeline --check + test_by_group_index_matches_matcher) proves the index equals the matcher and coverage is still 100%.

docs.title: Multi-agent skill workflow
docs.text: How multiple AI agents (or humans + AI) work on skills in parallel without stepping on each other -- and without anyone memorizing update procedures.

docs.title: The one rule
docs.text:
Edit DATA, then run ONE command. Never hand-edit GENERATED files.

python -m axiom_cli skills apply          # link -> enrich -> index -> clients -> validate
python -m axiom_cli skills apply --check  # verify only (what CI runs)

The same pipeline is one MCP call: skill_pipeline (apply=true to write, default is check-only). Tell the AI exactly this sentence:

"When you finish changing any skill, run skill_pipeline with apply=true. If it reports error, fix what it names and re-run. Do not hand-edit registries/, client mirrors, or catalog facets."

That single instruction replaces the old 5-script procedure. Forgetting a step is now impossible: there is only one step.

docs.title: Data vs generated (ownership map)
docs.text: Layer Files Who edits Parallel rule L0 skill content skills/<id>/SKILL.md, templates/, checklists/, scripts/, examples/ Any agent One skill dir per agent. Never two agents in the same dir. L1 relationships skills/catalog.yaml graph keys (related/extends/sub_skills/overlays) Agent owning the new skill Edit only your skill's entry via skills link --set; never touch others' entries. L2 catalog facets skills/catalog.yaml facet fields Nobody by hand enrich backfills from SKILL.md frontmatter. If a facet is wrong, fix the frontmatter, not the catalog. L3 generated registries/*.json, .opencode/*, .claude/*, .claude-plugin/*, GEMINI.md, copilot-instructions.md Nobody by hand Pipeline regenerates. The client mirrors are gitignored build outputs (rebuild with scripts/sync_clients.py after cloning); CI fails on drift in tracked files. L4 framework code packages/*, axiom_mcp/*, axiom_cli/*, scripts/* Senior agent/human only Adding a skill NEVER needs this. Only new tool kinds do.

docs.title: Parallel-work protocol
docs.text:
1. Claim a skill directory (one agent = one skills/<id>/ dir, or one domain subtree like skills/automotive/*). Your catalog graph entries are yours to edit via skills link --set.
  2. Scaffold, don't copy: axiom skills create <id> --title ... --apply (or MCP create_skill with apply=true), then write original content.
  3. Finish with the pipeline: run skills apply (CLI) or skill_pipeline apply=true (MCP). Green = mergeable. Red = the report names the exact file/field -- fix and re-run.
  4. Merge gate: a branch merges only when skills apply --check, pytest, and doctor are green. The pipeline is idempotent: re-running on a clean tree changes zero files, so concurrent agents can't corrupt each other through it.
  5. Conflicts: two agents editing different catalog entries merge cleanly (one YAML mapping per skill). If both touch one entry or one SKILL.md, that violates rule 1; reassign.

docs.title: Using skills for feature development (any domain)
docs.text:
Skills are consumers of the same pipeline, not just its product:

  • run_skill (CLI skills run, MCP) executes a skill as a structured workflow with dry-run default -- safe for an AI to propose, human to apply.
  • Generator tools (generate_checklist, generate_test_plan, generate_traceability_matrix, generate_report, review_configuration, analyze_trace, analyze_repository) turn skill content into reviewable artifacts during feature work.
  • engage(domain, platform) + install --domains scope an agent session to one domain: axiom install --client opencode --domains automotive copies only matching skills (plus domains=[all] shared skills); MCP discovery filters the same way at runtime.

docs.title: Why no .py edits as skills grow
docs.text:
• New skill -> data files only. Discovery (catalog, index, mirrors, agent configs) is derived by the pipeline.
  • New domain/platform binding -> frontmatter lists + pipeline. The install --domains filter reads the generated index, so it follows automatically.
  • New tool kind -> one function in packages/skill_tools.py + one TOOLS entry + tests. This is the only case that touches framework code, and it is deliberately rare (7 generators cover all 35 axiom-* skills today).
